items.stem: Which statement best gives the historical context for Locke's Two Treatises of Government, 1690?

options.1: Written after the French Revolution had overthrown the French king
options.2: Written the year after England forced out one king and installed another on terms
options.3: Written to defend the divine right of kings
options.4: Written in Russia to advise Catherine the Great

hints: Check the date. What had just happened in England?
The French Revolution is 1789, a hundred years later.
items.rationale: Locke published in 1690, the year after England replaced one king with another on terms. He wrote to justify it. The French Revolution came a century later.

items.stem: Which statement best gives the historical context for Montesquieu's The Spirit of the Laws, 1748?

options.1: Written after the U.S. Constitution had already split power into three branches
options.3: Written in France, where an absolute king held the power to make, enforce and judge the law
options.4: Written in Japan under the Tokugawa shogun

hints: Montesquieu was French. Who ruled France in 1748?
The U.S. Constitution came almost forty years later. It copied Montesquieu, not the other way around.
items.rationale: Montesquieu wrote in France under an absolute king who held every kind of power. That's why he argued for splitting it. The U.S. Constitution borrowed his idea in 1787.

items.stem: Which statement best gives the historical context for Wollstonecraft's A Vindication of the Rights of Woman, 1792?

options.1: Written while revolutionary France was writing new rules about rights that left women out
options.2: Written after women in Europe had already won the right to vote
options.3: Written to support the absolute rule of Louis XIV

hints: She wrote to a French lawmaker. What were French lawmakers writing?
items.rationale: Wollstonecraft wrote during the French Revolution, while France wrote new rules about rights. Women were left out, and she addressed the book to a French lawmaker to say so.

items.stem: Which statement best gives the historical context for Wilberforce's 1789 speech to Parliament?

options.1: Spoken after slavery had already ended everywhere in the British Empire
options.2: Spoken while British ships still carried enslaved Africans across the Atlantic
options.4: Spoken to celebrate the growth of the slave trade

hints: Wilberforce wanted to end something. Was it still going on in 1789?
He spoke in Britain's Parliament, not France's assembly.
items.rationale: In 1789 the British slave trade was still running. Wilberforce spoke in Parliament to demand that it be abolished.

items.stem: Which statement best gives the historical context for Catherine the Great's 1767 instructions for Russia's laws?

options.1: Written by an elected president of Russia
options.2: Written after Russia had freed its serfs
options.3: Written by a French philosophe living in exile
options.4: Written by an absolute ruler who admired the philosophes but kept millions of serfs

hints: Catherine was an empress. How did she come to power, and how much did she hold?
Russia's serfs weren't freed until long after Catherine died.
items.rationale: Catherine was an absolute ruler who read the philosophes and wrote about equal laws. Russia's serfs stayed bound to the land, and there were more of them when she died.
